NFL DFS Projections Week 8: DraftKings Picks, Values and Sim Plays

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 1 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 27, 4:33 PM ET

Jahmyr Gibbs carries the highest SPAGS model projection on the Week 8 DraftKings main slate: 27.8 DraftKings points at $9,500. He holds 28% of the simulated winning-lineup credit across 10,000 simulations. Chargers holds the largest share at 37% for $2,000.

Behind Gibbs, the model's next four projections are Puka Nacua (23.3, $8,600), Kenneth Walker III (22.9, $8,800), Josh Allen (22.5, $7,700) and Kyren Williams (21.2, $7,500). Jahmyr Gibbs returns the most per dollar of that group at 2.92 projected points per $1,000. Puka Nacua leads the wide receivers at 23.3 for $8,600, Josh Allen leads the quarterbacks at 22.5 for $7,700, and Trey McBride leads the tight ends at 19.7 for $7,400.

The 11-game slate runs from a 54.5-point total in ARI at DAL down to 39.5 in CLE at PIT. Every projection below is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 27, 4:33 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. Winning-lineup credit comes from 10,000 simulations of the contest, and tied winning entries share credit. A player's simulated floor is his 10th-percentile score and his ceiling is his 95th.

Quarterbacks: Week 8 DraftKings projections

Josh Allen, BUF vs BAL ($7,700)

Josh Allen carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 22.5 DraftKings points at $7,700, the 4th-highest on the entire main slate. That is 1.7 points clear of Dak Prescott. The model includes 6.7 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 2.92 projected points per $1,000, 17th of 21 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Allen averaged 22.5 points with a simulated floor of 8.4 and a ceiling of 40.5, and he holds 8% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Buffalo is a 3.5-point favorite at home against Baltimore, with an implied team total of 28.5 in a game totaled at 53.5.

Dak Prescott, DAL vs ARI ($6,300)

Dak Prescott projects 2nd at the position with 20.8 DraftKings points at $6,300. The salary works out to 3.29 projected points per $1,000, 6th of 21 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Prescott averaged 20.9 points with a simulated floor of 7.9 and a ceiling of 38.3, and he holds 15% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Dallas is a 6-point favorite at home against Arizona, with an implied team total of 30.25 in a game totaled at 54.5.

Value: Malik Willis, MIA vs NE ($4,900)

Malik Willis projects for 17.1 DraftKings points at $4,900, which works out to 3.50 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 21 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. The model includes 4.9 rushing attempts. Across 10,000 simulations Willis averaged 17.2 points with a simulated floor of 6.8 and a ceiling of 31.4, and he holds 3% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Miami is a 7.5-point underdog at home against New England, with an implied team total of 18.5 in a game totaled at 44.5.

Chase Brown projects for 18.3 DraftKings points at $6,300, which works out to 2.91 points per $1,000 of salary.
